opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexandra Johnson (employee ID E003) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E003.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin on Source Code. Full-time employees max is write unless their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code, so admin is not permitted. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write only with advanced training, never admin). Since admin is requested but not permitted, recommend granting read.
reason: Alexandra Johnson (E003) requests admin on Source Code. The HR note (full-time Analyst) permits up to write since Analyst does not own Source Code, while the Security note (contractor with basic security training) permits at most read and never admin. The employment-type records conflict, so I apply the more restrictive verified interpretation: contractor with basic training → maximum read. Admin is above that maximum, so grant read.
